A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLaID++ research work. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison; rendered figures resolve content not fully captured by text extraction. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original MP-20 crystal-generation experiments, model ablations, and DFT validation of 1,000 generated structures, including supplementary MLIP validation.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds original bulk-modulus and band-gap targeting results in Tables 2 and 4. Its separately attributed external benchmark is not needed to establish this assessment.

M1.justification: The Qwen-2.5-7B, Wyckoff representation, and iterative DPO pipeline remain intact. v4 adds property-specific adaptations: bulk-modulus preference pairs combined with existing objectives, and MEGNet-based band-gap preference tiers (Section 5.3 and Appendix 7.2). These extend the reward procedure without replacing the core method.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands beyond unconditional and space-group-conditioned generation to mechanical bulk-modulus and electronic band-gap targets. Appendix 7.4 also adds reported LeMat-GenBench evaluation using the broader LeMat-Bulk reference set. MP-20 training is retained; the eight unoptimized-space-group tests already existed in v3.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator set is retained. The new external comparison in Table 6 includes previously unevaluated WyFormer, WyFormer-DFT, DiffCSP++, and SymmCD, substantially broadening comparisons with symmetry-aware methods. Table 2 also introduces a bulk-modulus-only DPO comparator against joint optimization.

E3.justification: New property experiments use 1,000 generated samples, a 325–725 GPa bulk-modulus window, and band-gap success counts above 1, 2, and 3 eV. The token analysis samples MP-20 by crystal system. The external benchmark introduces a LeMat-Bulk reference and an MLIP ensemble. These are additional protocols, not demonstrated reruns of the retained MP-20 experiments.

E4.justification: v4 adds a bulk-modulus-only versus joint-objective ablation and examines token savings across symmetry classes (Tables 2 and 5). Existing temperature, DPO, representation, and MLIP validation analyses remain. The unoptimized-space-group results are relocated from v3 Figures 9–10 to v4 Figure 4 right and Figure 9, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for generation results. Existing MLIP–DFT regression reporting is retained. The new sample counts and MLIP ensemble do not establish a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial result entries: 40 high-bulk-modulus S.U.N. structures for joint training versus 28 for bulk-modulus-only training; band-gap counts of 15/9/3 versus the base model's 4/1/0; symmetry-stratified token counts; and external benchmark results of 12.4% stability and 1.0% S.U.N. for PLaID++. Main MP-20 and DFT results are unchanged. The external scores use different conditions and are not performance declines from v3.

T1.justification: The DPO objective, metric formulas, and Wyckoff mathematical background remain equivalent. The latter moves from Appendix 7.6 to 7.8. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central RLIP, Wyckoff-representation, and joint-training contributions are retained. The abstract strengthens the claimed advantage from approximately 50% to greater than 50%, although unchanged Table 1 reports 7.74% versus jointly trained ADiT's 5.3%, approximately 46%. Other abstract changes mainly emphasize claims already present in v3.

C2.justification: v4 interprets existing space-group transfer results as generalization beyond the reward structure, qualifies token savings for low-symmetry crystals, and discusses bulk-modulus outliers and stability–diversity tradeoffs under the external benchmark. It removes band-gap targeting from future work after adding that experiment and explains DPO's selection through expensive S.U.N. calculations.

D1.justification: Appendix 7.2 documents the new property evaluators, preference-pair construction, band-gap tiers, and bulk-modulus upper cutoff. Appendix 7.3 identifies the Qwen-2.5 tokenizer and stratified tokenization procedure. Existing LoRA, optimizer, hardware, and VASP configuration disclosures are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds CrystalICL to related work and positions its results against LeMat-GenBench. It also adds MEGNet, CIF, and VASP references. Existing Wyckoff Transformer and Matbench references receive publication updates rather than representing new research additions. The broader positioning narrative remains recognizable.

P1.justification: v4 selectively rewrites the abstract and conclusion, separates interpretation into Section 5.4, moves DFT validation within the results, and renames Section 6 from Discussion to Conclusion. Author order, affiliations, and acknowledgments also change. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays. Four tables are added. Figure 4 combines the previous main-text chart with appendix S.S.U.N. results and corrects its Unconditional Only legend to Spacegroup Only, matching the description already in v3. Other appendix figures are redrawn or relocated while retaining their results.

improvement.justification: The bulk-modulus and band-gap tests address v3's explicit limitation in property-targeted evaluation. The broader benchmark and symmetry-dependent token analysis also strengthen applicability evidence and clarify boundaries. These gains are limited by predictor-based property validation without uncertainty reporting, while the abstract's strengthened greater-than-50% wording does not match the approximately 46% margin in unchanged MP-20 Table 1. The additions provide useful, bounded improvements to an already extensively evaluated core.
